prompt: Gentle, slow movement therapy for seniors at home, NOT martial arts. The same woman, same studio, same clothes and lighting. She moves slowly and smoothly from the pose in the first frame to exactly the pose in the last frame, in one continuous motion, nothing else. The weight settles onto the rear leg and the front foot slides a little forward to rest on its toes. The rear-side hand floats up to eyebrow height, palm forward, while the other hand presses down beside the hip. Spine vertical. She stays TALL the whole time: her hips remain high, her knees are only softly unlocked (a slight bend of a few degrees, never a squat, never a lunge, never a deep stance), each knee stays above its own foot, the back heels stay on the floor, the spine is vertical, shoulders relaxed, chin level, calm gentle face, natural breathing. Static locked camera, no camera movement, no zoom, no cuts, full body always in frame from head to feet, feet visible on the floor, background unchanged.
